To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

DQf-D is an algorithm that leverages small amounts of demonstration (demonstrations from a human, another agent, a simulator, etc.) to accelerate the learning of a DQN and to learn to out-perform a given demonstrator.

DQf D is able to leverage small sets of demonstration to massively accelerate the deep Q-learning process and is able to assess the necessary ratio demonstration data while learning, and that DQf d is able to leverage human demonstration data to achieve state-ofthe- art results for 11 Atari games, while outperforming the best demonstrator in 14 of the 42 Atari games.
DQfD is the first algorithm to leverage human demonstrations to achieve the best known results on Atari games, and DQfD outperforms PDD DQN in the majority of the games.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to learn to perform a task from a small number of demonstrations.
the problem of learning from a small amount of expert data in the context of deep reinforcement learning.
how to improve the sample efficiency of deep Q-learning algorithms by using demonstration data.
